name: 仰卧4字拉伸
description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee so that your legs form a figure four. Reach through the gap and hold the back of the thigh of the lower leg, or its shin, and gently pull it towards your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute and outer hip of the crossed leg. Keep your head and lower back on the floor and let the crossed knee open outwards. Hold the stretch and breathe calmly, then switch sides.

name: 弹力带肩胛后缩
description: Attach one end of resistance band to wall/upright/... at shoulder height. Insert arm into the loop, at the tricep. Step back until band is pulled straight. Pull back elbow and shoulder against the resistance of the band.

name: 上斜哑铃Y举
description: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit facing the bench, chest against the pad, with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Position your feet firmly on the ground for stability and let your arms hang down naturally with a slight bend in your elbows. Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement. Raise your arms forward and out to form a Y shape, keeping the movement controlled and your elbows slightly bent. Lift until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor and in line with your ears. Pause briefly at the top of the movement to engage your shoulder muscles fully, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Ensure the movement is slow and controlled during both the ascent and descent to maximize engagement of the deltoids and supporting muscles. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.

name: 哑铃腕伸展
description: Grab two dumbbells with an overhand grip and lay your forearms across your knees. Let your wrists flex fully, then extend your wrists.

name: 高位绳索侧平举
description: Stand next to a cable machine with the pulley set to waist height. Grab the opposite-side handle with the hand farthest from the pulley, keeping your palm facing in. Keep your core engaged, chest lifted, and shoulders relaxed. Maintain a slight bend in the elbow throughout the lift. Lift your arm out to the side until your elbow reaches shoulder height, keeping your wrist aligned with your elbow. Briefly pause at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to your side with control. Repeat for the desired reps.

name: 坐箱内旋拉伸
description: Starting Position: Sit on the floor with both hips and knees bent at 90-degree angles. Leg Placement: Place one leg in front of you (external rotation) and the other leg out to the side/behind you (internal rotation). The shins and knees should remain flat on the ground. The Movement: Keeping your hips square, hinge your torso forward or tilt it laterally (side-to-side) toward the front leg to deepen the stretch. Target Areas: Stretches the glutes and piriformis (front leg) and the hip flexors and quads (back leg). Engages the core and obliques during lateral flexion. Goal: Improves hip mobility, specifically internal and external rotation, and relieves lower back tension.

name: YTWL字母操
description: Purpose: Improves shoulder stability, posture, and scapular (shoulder blade) control. Often used in physical therapy and warm-ups. Starting Position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips (like a deadlift) keeping your back flat, or lie face down on an incline bench. Keep your thumbs pointing up throughout. Y (Arms up): Extend both arms straight forward and upward at a 135-degree angle from your body, forming a "Y". Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. T (Arms out): Open your arms straight out to the sides, perpendicular to your body, forming a "T". Focus on pinching your shoulder blades. W (Arms bent): Pull your elbows back, bending them to 90 degrees, and squeeze your shoulder blades to form a "W". Keep your wrists firm. L (Arms rotated): Start with elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearms outward (external rotation) like a goalpost, forming an "L" or a gate. Key Focus: Movements should be slow and controlled. Always lead with the thumbs and think about moving the shoulder blades, not just the arms.

name: 仰卧髋外展
description: Starting Position: Lie on your back (supine) on a mat, with your legs extended and relaxed. Arms can be placed alongside your body or out to the sides for stability. The Movement: Slightly lift one leg off the floor (keeping it straight or with a slight bend). Move it laterally outward, away from the other leg, as if stepping over a small obstacle. Range of Motion: Move the leg as far as comfortable without lifting your pelvis or rotating your torso, feeling a stretch in the inner thigh and hip. Return: Slowly bring the leg back to the starting position with controlled movement. Goal: Improves lateral hip mobility (abduction) and strengthens the pelvic stabilizer muscles.

name: 下斜凳抬腿
description: Setup: Lie on a decline bench with your head at the top and grip the handles. The Start: Extend legs fully, keeping them slightly elevated to engage your core. The Lift: Raise your legs toward the ceiling using your abs, not momentum. The Squeeze: Pause and contract your lower abdominals at the top. The Return: Lower your legs slowly to the starting position with control.

name: 杠铃过顶推举
description: Setup: Stand with feet together and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders. Position: Rest the bar on your upper chest. Press: Brace your core and push the bar straight up until your arms lock out. Finish: Control the bar back down to your chest. https://youtu.be/ZXpdJOLNoWw?si=u27cGyODoblXHBu1

name: 绳索三头下压
description: Setup: Stand facing the cable, feet shoulder-width apart, with a slight forward lean. Grip: Hold the rope with palms facing each other and elbows tucked tight to your ribs. Execution: Push the rope down until arms are fully straight, pulling the ends apart at the bottom. Control: Keep upper arms still and return to the start with a slow, controlled motion.

name: 翻举接推举
description: The First Pull: Lift the bar from the floor to knee-height by driving with the legs, keeping the angle of your back constant. The "Power" Position: As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively shrug and extend your hips to create vertical momentum. The Quick Elbow Turnover: In the catch phase, rotate your elbows rapidly under the bar to create a "shelf" on your front deltoids. The Vertical Press: Press the bar in a straight line; your head should shift slightly forward once the bar clears your forehead to reach full lockout.

name: 负重俯卧撑
description: Setup: Begin in a standard plank position with a weight plate balanced securely on your upper back. Alignment: Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, engaging your core to prevent your back from sagging. Execution: Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your elbows at a forty-five degrees. Ascent: Press through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

name: 蝴蝶机夹胸
description: Pectoral issolation exercise - full range of motion is best with full contraction and slow negative

name: 后拉
description: Set weight and grip for the cables in the cage. Take a few steps away, bend over, pull and extend the back at the same time.

name: 髋桥
description: Get into bridge position, balance yourself on heels and start extending legs unilaterally. Keep hip extended as much as possible.

name: 单侧弓步蹲
description: No stops during movement, hands on the hips.

name: 蝴蝶式超人
description: Lie on stomach, intertwine fingers behind the head and start raising your head and raise elbows as far as they go.

name: 腿轮
description: Lay on the back and lift legs in perpendicular fashion, keeping the knees together. Start making small circles in one direction with both of your knees with very small range of motion, focusing on abs and keeping your back in contact with the floor.

name: 跪姿超人式
description: Push one foot back until leg fully extended, concentrating on the having the foot high and pushed back as if pulled. Extend arm forward with focus having the shoulder high up. Unilateral and static hold.

name: 猫式平板
description: On your fours and raise the knees of the floor ever so slightly. Curl your back out and push back from your shoulders as to resemble a cat making itself look large.

name: 核心旋转
description: Sit back, raise feet above the ground with knees bent and start rotating left and right with hands touching the ground every move.

name: 单侧臀推
description: Extend one leg while laying down and start raising your body with one leg touching the ground through the heel.

name: 双杠等长保持
description: The parallel bars isometric hold is a static upper-body exercise performed on dip bars (parallel bars). Instead of moving up and down like in a traditional dip, you hold a fixed position under tension.

name: 四足髋外展
description: Distribute your body weight evenly on all knees and arms. Keep the torso stable, with the abdomen engaged and the lumbar spine straight without twisting the back (imagine: a glass on your lower back won't fall off). Raise one leg outwards without twisting it. Pay attention to the right angle at the hips and knees. Always train both sides of the body. To increase resistance, a resistance band can be used.

name: 团身俄挺
description: Basic calisthenics progression for the full planche

name: Legend推胸
description: Plate-loaded chest press machine from Legend Fitness LeverEdge line.

name: 深度胸肌拉伸
description: Deep loaded stretch for pectorals, typically performed at end of chest work.

name: 深度肩部拉伸
description: Deep loaded stretch for deltoids, performed after pressing movements.

name: 深度背阔肌拉伸
description: Deep loaded stretch for latissimus dorsi, performed after pulling movements.

name: 坐姿绳索夹胸
description: Place a bench between two cable pulleys and adjust the pulleys so they are at chest/shoulder height when you are seated. Grab the handles with a neutral grip and lean against the upright backrest. Bring your arms together in front of your chest in a controlled motion, focusing on squeezing your chest muscles. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement. Pause briefly at the top position. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position while maintaining control of the movement. Repeat for reps.

Bend forward at the hips with a slight bend in your knees, keeping your back straight. Engage your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to touch them together. Release the shrug. Description taken from MuscleWiki

name: 反向高位下拉
description: The Inverted Lat Pull Down (most commonly known as the Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down) is a variation of the standard exercise that uses an underhand (supinated) grip with hands at shoulder-width. This position shifts more emphasis to the lower lats and increases biceps involvement, often allowing for a greater range of motion and a deeper squeeze at the bottom of the movement.

name: 坐姿V把划船
description: The Seated V-Grip Row is a compound pulling exercise performed on a cable machine using a close-grip "V" handle. While seated with your feet braced, you pull the handle toward your midsection, focusing on back thickness and mid-back development.

name: 辅助引体向上
description: The Assisted Pull-Up is a compound vertical pulling exercise performed on a machine with a counterweight platform or by using resistance bands. It mimics the mechanics of a standard pull-up but reduces the total weight you have to lift, making it an excellent tool for building functional strength and perfecting your technique.

name: 哑铃弯举
description: The Dumbbell Curl is a classic isolation exercise for the arms. Unlike the Hammer Curl, it involves rotating your wrists (supination) as you lift the weights, which allows for a full contraction of the biceps.

name: 腹部卷腹
description: The Abdominal Crunch is a classic core isolation exercise performed on the floor or a mat. Unlike a full sit-up, it involves a smaller range of motion where you only lift your shoulders and upper back off the ground, keeping your lower back pressed firmly against the floor.

name: 腰带深蹲
description: Belt Squat: a squat variation done with a belt attached to a loading machine or platform so the weight is supported at the hips instead of on the spine. It mainly trains the quads and glutes, with much less lower-back fatigue than a barbell squat. Use a full range of motion, keep the torso upright, and drive through the mid-foot.

name: 绳索单臂后束飞鸟
description: Cable rear delt fly (single arm): Stand sideways to a cable machine with the handle set around shoulder height. With a slight bend in the elbow, pull the handle out and back in a wide arc so the upper arm moves away from the body. Keep your torso still and focus on the rear delt doing the work. Use light to moderate weight and controlled reps.

name: 猫牛式
description: On all fours. Arch spine up (cat) then drop it down (cow). Breathe with movement.

name: 颈部可控关节旋转
description: Controlled Articular Rotations. Slow full circles 3 each way. Cervical mobility.

name: 膈式呼吸
description: Belly breathing. Hand on chest stays still, hand on belly rises. 8-10 slow breaths.

name: 哑铃抓举
description: Key Steps to Execute Correctly: Setup: Place the dumbbell between your feet, with your shoulders above your hips, chest up, and back flat. The Pull: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) to drive the dumbbell upward, keeping your elbow high and the dumbbell close to your body. The Catch: Quickly flex your hips and knees to drop under the dumbbell and receive it overhead with your arm locked in position, landing in a half-squat stance. Common Mistakes: Using your arms too much to lift the weight instead of your legs, having a low elbow during the pull phase, and misaligning your shoulder, elbow, and wrist in the final position. For beginners, it’s recommended to start with light loads, focus on technique, and perform 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 5 reps per arm.

name: 单腿箱式深蹲
description: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.

name: 开合步
description: The Step Jack is a low-impact plyometric-style move that provides cardiovascular benefits without the joint stress of jumping. It works the entire body, specifically targeting the legs, core, and shoulders. This move is ideal for beginners, individuals with joint sensitivities, or as a dynamic warm-up to gradually elevate the heart rate. Notes (Instructions): ​Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides. ​Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms up above your head. Bring your right foot back to the center and lower your arms. ​Immediately repeat the movement, stepping out with your left foot. ​Continue alternating sides at a steady, rhythmic pace.

name: 慢速深蹲
description: ​A tempo-based squat that uses controlled movement to increase muscle tension and improve lower-body stability. ​Lower: Descend slowly for 3 seconds. ​Pause: Hold at the bottom for 1 second. ​Stand: Return to the starting position at a normal pace. Form: Keep your chest up and weight in your heels.

name: 宽距俯卧撑
description: ​A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to increase the emphasis on the outer chest muscles and shoulders. ​Setup: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor. Lower: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your core tight. ​Push: Drive through your palms to return to the start position. ​Form: Don't let your lower back sag; keep a straight line from head to heels.

name: 踏步高抬腿
description: A low-impact cardio and mobility exercise that strengthens the hip flexors and improves balance. ​Movement: Stand tall and lift one knee toward your chest as high as comfortable. ​Arms: Swing the opposite arm forward as you lift your knee, similar to a walking motion. ​Core: Keep your abs engaged to maintain an upright posture. ​Pace: Perform the movement with control, alternating legs rhythmically.

name: 半跪胸椎旋转
description: Begin in a half kneeling position with the leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall with a ball. With both hands directly in front of you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach the wall behind you. Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return to neutral and repeat.

name: 坐姿慢速推举
description: slow controlled seated forward exercise with dumbbells

name: 单臂哑铃推肩
description: Press the dumbbell vertically overhead in a controlled motion until your arm is fully extended, without locking the elbow. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.

name: 单臂绳索下压
description: Single-arm cable pushdown is a unilateral isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii. By working one arm at a time, it helps correct strength imbalances between sides while also engaging the core for stability. Starting position: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a single handle to the high pulley. Grab the handle with one hand using an overhand grip (pronated), with your elbow bent at approximately 90° and tucked close to your body. Keep your core braced and your back straight. Execution: Push the handle downward in a controlled motion by extending your elbow until your arm is fully extended. Hold the contraction for 1 second at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.

name: 壶铃相扑高拉
description: A compound exercise combining elements of a sumo deadlift and a high pull. It targets the posterior chain, particularly the glutes, hamstrings, and upper back. The sumo stance increases hip engagement, while the high pull adds an explosive element, promoting power development. Stand upright overtop of a kettlebell with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart angled out slightly. Maintain a braced core and neutral spine throughout the exercise. Hinge your hips backward and extend your arms to grab ahold the kettlebell with a double overhand grip. With you lower legs nearly vertical to the ground, extend your hips to raise the kettlebell with your elbows high keeping it close to your body. Once the kettlebell has reached shoulder height, lower back to the starting position.

name: 门泽尔下拉
description: Close grip front facing Pull down, while focusing on Biceps, Increases activation of biceps over the whole range, Avoid activating Lats.

name: 单臂高位下拉
description: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and grab the single handle with a neutral grip. Keep your torso stable, your chest lifted, and your shoulder blades slightly retracted. Start with your arm fully extended overhead, then pull the handle down toward your upper chest following a controlled, slightly diagonal path. Focus on engaging the latissimus dorsi while keeping the shoulder depressed and avoiding any torso rotation. Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining full control throughout the movement.

name: 髋部飞机式
description: Stand on one leg and lean your upper body slightly forward while keeping your back straight. Extend the free leg behind you so that your torso and leg form roughly one line. Slowly open your hip to the side by rotating your pelvis and upper body in a controlled way. Then close the hip again and return to the starting position. The movement should mainly come from the hip. Keep your standing foot stable and avoid letting your knee collapse inward.

name: 反向蚌式
description: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your knees stacked on top of each other. Keep your feet together at first, then keep your knees touching while lifting your top foot upward. Slowly lower the foot back down with control. Move only through the hip and avoid rolling your pelvis backward. The movement should be small, controlled, and focused on hip rotation.

name: 蚌式接反向蚌式
description: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your legs stacked. Lift your top knee into a clamshell position and keep the leg elevated throughout the movement. From there, alternate between opening the knee upward and lifting the foot upward, moving through hip external and internal rotation. Keep the movement slow and controlled. Do not let the top leg rest on the bottom leg between repetitions.

name: 杠铃腕弯举
description: This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso. Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders. Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch. Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second. Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.

name: YTW举
description: The YTW exercise for scapular retraction is designed to strengthen the inter-scapular muscles between your shoulder blades, to help retract or pull your shoulders back, helping to maintain proper upright posture.

name: 臀腘弯举
description: Kneel on a glute-ham developer or have a partner hold your ankles. Keeping hips straight, lower your torso toward the floor under control, then curl back up by contracting the hamstrings and glutes.

name: 轻松连续自由泳
description: Swim freestyle at a relaxed, steady pace without stopping — think conversation pace, not racing. Focus on smooth, even strokes rather than speed or breathing technique; this is just to get your body moving and your heart rate up.

name: 扶板打腿
description: Hold a kickboard with both hands, arms extended in front of you, face in the water (lift head forward to breathe when needed). Kick from your hips, not your knees, keeping your legs mostly straight with a slight bend and a steady, compact flutter kick. This builds leg endurance and keeps your body horizontal without needing to worry about your arms.

name: 浮沉呼气练习
description: Stand in chest-deep water. Take a breath, submerge your face fully, and exhale slowly and completely through your nose and/or mouth the whole time you're underwater — a gentle humming sound can help keep the exhale steady and controlled. Once you're empty of air, lift your head, take a fresh breath, and go back under. Repeat continuously. The goal is training your body that all your exhaling happens underwater, so all you need to do at the surface is inhale.

name: 扶墙转体
description: Hold the pool wall or edge with one hand, body horizontal at the surface, legs kicking gently behind you. Keep your face in the water, exhaling continuously, then rotate your head to the side — not lifting it up — so one goggle stays in the water while the other clears the surface. Take a quick breath, then rotate your face back down to neutral. This isolates the head-rotation motion without any arm strokes to think about.

name: 扶板侧踢呼吸
description: Push off the wall on your side (not flat on your stomach), one arm extended forward holding the board or just extended, kicking continuously. Keep your head in a neutral position looking at the bottom of the pool, and when you need air, rotate your head sideways (one ear stays in the water, other faces up) to breathe, then rotate back to neutral. Swim a length like this, then repeat on the other side. This teaches the exact head position and rotation you'll use once full stroke breathing comes in.

name: 划水转体练习
description: Push off, swim a few strokes, and every breath roll fully onto your back for 2-3 breaths, then roll back into freestyle. This teaches you to rotate your body as a unit rather than just turning your head, and helps remove the fear of not having your face in the water.

name: 恢复性浮沉
description: Same motion as the Bobbing Exhale Drill, but done in slightly deeper water (so you're not touching the bottom) and at a slower, more relaxed pace — think of it as a recovery/reset exercise rather than a hard drill. Use it between harder drills to reset your breathing rhythm and calm down if you're feeling rushed or out of sync.

name: 放松游
description: Swim at an easy, unhurried pace — freestyle, backstroke, or just floating/gliding — with zero focus on technique or drills. The only goal here is to let your heart rate come down gradually and your muscles relax before you get out of the pool.

name: 骨盆后倾
description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Flatten your lower back against the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, engaging your abs and glutes. Hold 5 seconds, release. This retrains pelvic positioning to counter anterior pelvic tilt.

name: 弹力带终末伸膝
description: This is an end range strengthening exercise for the knee extensors. Start by looping a band around the back of one knee and anchoring the other end to a stable surface in front of you. Stand in a split stance with the banded knee bent and placed as the front leg. Straighten the knee to pull against the bands resistance and maintain a contraction in your quadriceps for up to 5 seconds before releasing.

name: 前锯肌靠墙滑动拉伸
description: Stand facing a wall. Place your forearms vertically against the wall so your elbows and wrists are both touching it. Point your arms slightly outwards from "straight up". Protract your shoulders hard, then slide your forearms up the wall until your elbows are about level with your chin. Slide your forearms back down the wall. Repeat as necessary.

name: 沙发拉伸
description: Stand facing away from a bench, couch or similar-height object. Extend one leg backwards, resting your foot "laces-down" on the edge of the bench. Lower yourself until your rear knee is on the floor and you are in a lunge position, with your torso hanging forwards slightly. Brace your core, tense your rear glute, and straighten up your torso to vertical, under control. Relax and repeat. Repeat for the other leg, too.

name: 长弓步弹动拉伸
description: Hold the resistance band (or any other rope-like object, the elasticity is not necessary) above your head, between your hands, with your arms straight. Pull it taught to engage your lats. Step forwards into a lunge, dropping until your knee is almost touching the floor. Slowly and controlledly pulse your body up and down by about an inch. Repeat for required reps. Repeat for other leg.

name: 前劈叉拉伸
description: Start kneeling. Extend one leg out forwards, fully straightened. Follow with your hips so your back leg begins to unfold. Carefully lower yourself into the stretch. Do not go beyond your limit. Hold for the required time.

name: 深蹲向天伸展
description: Drop into a squat. Hold one ankle with the opposite hand. Fold your other arm to your chest. Staying in the squat and keeping hold of your ankle, twist to turn your chest-hand back/outwards until your elbow is pointing at the sky. Return to the neutral squatting position with your hand on your chest. Repeat movement as required. Repeat on both sides.

name: 爆发俯卧撑
description: Explosive Push-Ups Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

name: 俄式俯卧撑
description: Russian Push-Ups Start in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift your body forward while keeping your chest close to the ground. Extend your arms to return to the starting position, then reverse the movement smoothly. Keep your core tight and maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise.

name: 肘杠杆
description: ​A calisthenics static balance skill where the entire body is held straight and parallel to the ground, supported by tucking the elbows firmly into the abdomen or pelvic bones.

name: 俄挺前倾保持
description: A straight-arm calisthenics static hold where you assume a plank position and lean the shoulders as far forward as possible past the wrists with protracted scapulae and a hollow body.

name: 弓身悬垂
description: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C995b3KLXS4&t=7s Elbows should stay straight Hold it for time/reps Start at an active hang: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HoE-C85ZlCE Progress towards a 90 degree in your shoulder

name: 腿屈伸等长保持
description: An isometric leg extension is a strengthening exercise where you contract your quadriceps muscles against an immovable resistance without changing the length of the muscle or moving your knee joint.

name: 卧推等长保持
description: A bench press isometric hold is a static strength exercise where you pause and hold a barbell or dumbbells either at your chest, mid-press, or at lockout without moving for a set time

name: 过顶推举等长保持
description: An isometric overhead press involves holding a weight statically overhead or pushing against an immovable object at a specific point in the press without moving the joint.

name: 侧平举等长保持
description: An isometric lateral raise is a shoulder exercise where you hold your arms out to the sides at waist height for a set amount of time instead of moving up and down

name: 牧师凳弯举等长保持
description: An isometric preacher curl is a static strength exercise where you hold a fixed position on a preacher pad or and inclined bench under tension without moving the joint.

name: 高位下拉等长保持
description: An isometric Lat pulldown is a strength-building exercise where you pull the bar down to your chest and hold the contracted position at the bottom without moving your limbs for a set number of seconds

name: 三头下压等长保持
description: A single-arm isometric or isolated triceps pushdown is an isolation cable exercise where you pin your upper arm against your torso, hinge at the hips, and extend the elbow to achieve a peak contraction in the triceps muscle.

name: 拳击
description: Bag workout for boxing skill development and cardio improvement

name: 手腕绕环
description: Wrist circles is warm-up exercise, where you rotate your wrists in a circular motion. They improve mobility and are recommended before exercises such as pull ups, hand stands and other exercises that put pressure on your wrists.

name: 跑步机倒走
description: Controlled treadmill walking performed backward, at a slow and steady speed. A slight incline of about 2 to 3 percent can be added if tolerated.

name: 凯格尔运动
description: Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit upright in a chair. Locate the pelvic floor muscles: they are the muscles you would use to stop the flow of urine or to hold back gas. Keep your abdomen, glutes and thighs relaxed and breathe normally throughout. Tighten the pelvic floor muscles and lift them gently upwards and inwards. Hold the contraction for a few seconds, then release completely and rest for at least as long as you held. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. The exercise can be varied by holding longer with a light contraction (endurance) or by performing quick, short contractions with a full relaxation in between.

name: 支撑分腿蹲
description: Stand in a split stance with one foot about a stride in front of the other, and hold on to a stable support such as a rack, a wall or the back of a chair. Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees until the back knee almost touches the floor. Keep your upper body upright and the front heel on the floor, then push through the front foot back up. Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up. Complete all repetitions, then switch sides.

name: 90/90呼吸
description: Controlled breathing drill performed in a 90/90 position to encourage rib, abdominal, and pelvic coordination.

name: 90/90髋部转换
description: Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor. Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions. Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

name: 内收肌后摇
description: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward. Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs. Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.

name: 抬高腘绳肌拉伸
description: Stand facing a bar, box or bench at roughly hip height and place the heel of one leg on it. Keep that leg straight with the toes pointing up, and keep the standing leg straight with both hips square to the support. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch in the back of the elevated thigh. Hold the position while breathing calmly, then switch legs. Stretch for the hamstrings. The height of the support controls the intensity: the higher the leg, the stronger the stretch.

name: BOSU单腿平衡
description: Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise The exercise for balancing on a BOSU ball while standing on one leg is known as the single-leg BOSU balance exercise. This exercise is effective for enhancing balance, coordination, and core stability. Benefits of the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise Improves Balance: Standing on one leg challenges your stability. Enhances Coordination: Engaging different muscle groups helps improve overall coordination. Strengthens Core: The exercise activates core muscles, promoting better posture and stability. How to Perform the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise Positioning: Stand on the dome side of the BOSU ball with one leg. Balance: Keep your opposite leg lifted and your core engaged. Duration: Aim to hold the position for 10-20 seconds, gradually increasing the time as you improve. Progression Tips Add Movement: Try reaching for objects around you while maintaining balance. Close Your Eyes: This increases the challenge by removing visual stability cues. Use a Ball: Catch or toss a ball while balancing to further engage your core and coordination. This exercise is a great way to build foundational balance skills before progressing to more complex movements.

name: 股四头肌等长收缩
description: What Are Quad Sets? Quad sets are a fundamental exercise used in knee rehabilitation. They focus on strengthening the quadriceps muscles located at the front of the thigh. This exercise is particularly beneficial for individuals recovering from knee injuries or surgeries. How to Perform Quad Sets Steps to Execute Quad Sets Positioning: Sit or lie down with your legs straight. Tightening: Tighten the quadriceps muscles while keeping the leg straight. You should see the kneecap move upward. Holding: Maintain the contraction for about 5 seconds. Releasing: Relax the muscle after the hold. Repetitions: Aim for 10 to 15 repetitions, gradually increasing as strength improves. Tips for Effective Quad Sets Ensure no other muscles are contracting to assist the quadriceps. Perform the exercise on a flat surface, like a bed or couch, with a towel or pillow under your heel for comfort. It is recommended to do these exercises multiple times a day, especially during the early stages of recovery. Benefits of Quad Sets Restores Muscle Function: Helps rebuild strength in the quadriceps. Improves Stability: Enhances stability in the knee joint. Increases Range of Motion: Aids in regaining mobility after injury or surgery. Incorporating quad sets into your rehabilitation routine can significantly aid in recovery and improve overall knee function.

name: 髋外展内收侧步
description: Overview of Hip-Out and Hip-In Lateral Steps Hip-out and hip-in lateral steps are effective exercises designed to strengthen the hip abductors and enhance lateral stability. These movements are beneficial for improving coordination and overall hip function. Exercise Descriptions Hip-Out Steps Movement: Step out to the side with one leg, keeping the other leg stable. Target Muscles: Primarily engages the hip abductors, including the gluteus medius and minimus. Benefits: Increases lateral stability and strength in the hip area. Hip-In Steps Movement: Bring the leg back in toward the center after stepping out. Target Muscles: Continues to engage the hip abductors while also activating the adductors. Benefits: Enhances coordination and control of the hip joint. Key Benefits of Lateral Steps | Benefit | Description | |---|---| | Strengthening Hip Abductors | Improves muscle strength around the hip joint. | | Enhancing Stability | Increases lateral stability, reducing the risk of falls. | | Improving Coordination | Develops better control and movement patterns in the hips. | Incorporating hip-out and hip-in lateral steps into a regular exercise routine can lead to improved hip strength and stability, which is essential for various physical activities and daily movements.

name: 单腿软着陆保持
description: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises that focus on balance and stability by landing softly on one leg and holding the position. This exercise helps improve proprioception and can be beneficial for rehabilitation and athletic training. Overview Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises designed to enhance balance, stability, and proprioception. They involve landing softly on one leg and maintaining that position for a brief period. This exercise is particularly useful in rehabilitation settings and for athletes looking to improve their performance. Benefits Improves balance: Enhances stability by training the body to control weight distribution on one leg. Enhances proprioception: Increases awareness of body position, which is crucial for injury prevention. Supports rehabilitation: Helps individuals recover from lower-limb injuries by strengthening muscles and improving joint stability. How to Perform Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds Steps Preparation: Stand on a stable surface or a box. Takeoff: Step off the box or surface with one leg, ensuring that you do not jump. Landing: Land softly on the target leg, allowing the knee and hip to bend slightly. Hold position: Maintain balance in the landed position for up to 2 seconds. Reset: Return to the starting position and repeat. Key Points to Remember Keep your chest up and engage your core for better stability. Ensure your knee aligns with the midline of your foot during landing. Focus on a con

name: 反向V蹲
description: Step into the V-squat machine facing the pad, the opposite way from the regular V-squat, so that your chest rests against the pad and your shoulders sit under the shoulder pads. Place your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart and release the safety. Brace your core and lower yourself by bending your knees and pushing the hips back until your thighs are roughly parallel to the platform. Drive back up through the heels without locking out the knees. Compared to the regular V-squat, the reversed position shifts the emphasis towards the glutes and hamstrings.

name: 箱上倒立撑
description: Pike push-up with legs on an elevated surface. Progression to handstand push-up.

name: 弹力带前平举
description: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet about hip-width apart, holding one end in each hand in front of your thighs. Keeping your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows, raise your hands forward to shoulder height, then lower slowly under control. Can be done with both arms together or alternating. Use a heavier band or shorten the band to increase resistance.

name: 挂片式高位下拉
description: Sit at a plate-loaded (lever) lat pulldown machine with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the handles overhead with arms fully extended. Pull the handles down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your lats at the bottom. Return slowly to full extension. Resistance comes from weight plates loaded on the machine's lever arms rather than a cable stack.

name: 侧倾绳索侧平举
description: Set a cable pulley at the lowest position and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine, hold the frame with your near hand and lean your body away so you hang at an angle. With the far hand, grasp the handle in front of your hips and raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow. Lower slowly. The lean increases tension on the side delts at the bottom of the movement. Complete all reps, then switch sides.

name: 牧师凳弯举机
description: Adjust the seat so that your armpits rest on the top edge of the pad and your upper arms lie flat on it. Grip the handles with your palms facing up. Curl the handles up by bending your elbows, without lifting your upper arms off the pad or leaning back. Squeeze the biceps briefly at the top, then lower the handles slowly until your arms are almost straight.

name: 坐姿弹力带划船
description: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you and your back tall. Loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet and hold one end in each hand, arms extended and a slight bend in the knees. Pull the band toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows straight back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your chest up and your torso still rather than rocking backward to move the band. Extend the arms slowly to return. Because the torso stays upright and supported, this is a useful row when a bent-over position is uncomfortable, and it needs no anchor point.

name: 柔性棒腕伸展
description: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing down and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist drop, then extend the wrist to raise the bar, keeping the forearm still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. The resistance comes from twisting or bending the flexible bar, so a thicker or stiffer bar increases the load. Commonly used for wrist and forearm strengthening and for elbow tendon rehabilitation.

name: 柔性棒腕屈曲
description: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist extend back, then curl the wrist up to raise the bar while the forearm stays still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. Works the wrist flexors, and is the companion movement to FlexBar wrist extension for balanced forearm strengthening.

name: 柔性棒泰勒扭转
description: An eccentric exercise for the wrist extensors, done with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar, and widely used in rehabilitation for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Hold the bar vertically in the affected hand with the wrist extended. Grasp the top of the bar with the other hand, palm facing away, and twist the top hand to wind up the bar. Bring both arms out in front of you with the bar horizontal, then slowly let the affected wrist untwist the bar over about four seconds while the other hand holds steady. Reset and repeat. The reverse version, twisting in the opposite direction for the wrist flexors, is used for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). Move slowly and stop if the exercise causes sharp pain rather than the expected mild discomfort.

name: 深蹲起立协调
description: Custom description created by the Integrated Conditioning routine importer for wger.

name: 温和反向凯格尔
description: Lie on your back with your knees bent, or sit comfortably. Breathe in slowly into your belly and let your pelvic floor relax and gently lengthen downwards, without pushing or straining. Breathe out and let the pelvic floor return to its resting position. Repeat slowly for several breaths. The reverse Kegel trains relaxing the pelvic floor, the opposite of the contraction in a regular Kegel exercise.

name: 快乐婴儿式
description: Lie on your back and pull your knees towards your armpits. Hold the outside of your feet, your ankles or your shins, with the soles of your feet facing the ceiling and your shins roughly vertical. Gently pull your feet down to open the hips while keeping your lower back and head on the floor. Hold the position and breathe calmly, you can also rock gently from side to side.

name: 哑铃提踵
description: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides and feet hip-width apart. For a larger range of motion, stand with the balls of your feet on a step or a weight plate. Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause briefly at the top. Then lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves. Keep your knees straight but not locked and your upper body upright.

name: 暂停深蹲
description: Use the same technic as your normal squat. Except that you make a pause at the bottom of the squat for about 1-2 seconds, in other words a bit longer than your normal squat.

name: 单臂绳索划船接转体（地板）
description: Go into a one-legged kneeling position and grab the cable from the lowest position. Rotate the upper torso to get into the starting position and bend the upper torso a little bit sidewise. Place the unused hand on the knee. Pull the cable while rotating the upper torso.

name: 坐姿加压伸膝
description: A gentle stretch to restore full knee extension. Sit with one leg stretched out in front of you and the heel propped on the floor or a low surface, so the knee is unsupported. Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap. Keeping the leg relaxed, gently press down through the hands toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee, and hold for about three seconds before releasing. The pressure should produce a stretch, never sharp pain. Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: 弹力带怪兽走
description: A banded walking drill for the glutes and hip stabilisers. Place a mini band around both thighs just above the knees, or around the ankles for a harder version. Stand with feet hip-width apart so the band is under tension, then sink into a quarter-squat with the chest up. Walk forward with small diagonal steps, pushing each leg out against the band and keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than letting them fall inward. Walk forward for the prescribed number of steps, then walk backward to return, keeping the band under tension throughout.

name: 台阶小腿拉伸
description: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.

name: 闭眼单腿平衡
description: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.

name: 单腿平衡壶铃绕环
description: A balance drill that adds a moving load. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand. Pass the kettlebell around your body in a circle, handing it from one hand to the other in front and behind you, while keeping your balance on the standing leg. Keep the hips level and the torso upright; the shifting weight of the bell constantly changes your centre of mass, which is what trains the hip and ankle stabilisers. Complete the prescribed number of circles, reverse direction, then switch legs. Use a light bell to start.

name: 俯身双臂哑铃划船
description: How to Perform It Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral or overhand grip. Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back, until your torso is roughly 45–75 degrees to the floor. Keep a slight bend in your knees. Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders with arms fully extended. Keep your back flat, chest up, and core braced — avoid rounding your spine. Pull the dumbbells up toward your ribcage/hips, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. Pause briefly at the top of the movement. Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Key Coaching Cues Hinge from the hips, not the lower back Keep the spine neutral throughout — no rounding Lead with the elbows, not the hands Avoid using momentum or jerking the weight up Control the eccentric (lowering) phase rather than letting the weights drop

name: 交替行走
description: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat

name: 广播体操
description: Video can be found here : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGPBSqxKGAc Full-body mobility and dynamic warm-up routine (3–5 minutes) to prepare joints, muscles, and the cardiovascular system for workout. Movement Flow: Deep Breathing & Arm Raises: Inhale while raising arms laterally overhead, exhale as you lower them. Knee Bends: Soft, rhythmic knee flexions synchronized with arm swings. Arm Circles: Large full-range arm rotations forward, then backward to open up the chest and shoulder girdle. Chest Expansion: Cross arms in front of the chest and open wide to the sides. Side Bends: Reach overhead to stretch the lateral torso left and right with a smooth side flexion. Forward & Back Bends: Gently hinge at the hips to reach forward, then return upright with a mild spinal extension. Torso Twists: Swing arms side-to-side to rotate the spine and loosen the core. Ankle Mobility / Light Bounces: Soft heel lifts or light bouncing on toes to warm up lower leg joints and tendons.

name: 凯尔索耸肩
description: Kelso shrugs are a variation of scapular shrugs designed primarily to train scapular retraction, with particular emphasis on the middle trapezius, rhomboids, and, secondarily, the lower trapezius. Unlike conventional shrugs, the goal is not to elevate the shoulders toward the ears, but rather to pull the shoulder blades backward. They are typically performed with the chest supported on an incline bench, using either dumbbells or a barbell: Lie face down on an incline bench, with your arms extended toward the floor. Keep your elbows almost completely locked throughout the movement. Starting with the shoulder blades slightly protracted, retract them, trying to bring them closer together. Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench; avoid turning the movement into a row by extending your torso. Briefly hold the fully retracted position, then return in a controlled manner, allowing the shoulder blades to separate.

name: 真空吸腹
description: Starting position: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor (or stand/sit upright). Exhalation: Fully exhale all the air from your lungs through your mouth. Contraction: Draw your navel in towards your spine as far as possible, pulling your stomach inward and up under your ribcage. Hold: Hold this isometric contraction without breathing for 10 to 20 seconds. Release: Slowly inhale through your nose to release the tension and relax your abdominals. Repeat: Rest briefly and perform the desired number of sets.

name: 船长椅提膝
description: Starting position Step into the captain's chair (vertical knee raise station). Rest your forearms on the pads and hold the handles. Keep your upper body upright, look straight ahead and press your back against the pad, without rounding or arching it. Your legs are almost straight with a slight bend in the knees, your feet are off the floor and your legs are together. Movement Pull your bent legs up, bringing your knees towards your chest. Only go as high as you can while keeping good form, with your legs together the whole time. Then lower your legs again while inhaling, without putting your feet back on the floor.

name: 船长椅侧提膝
description: Starting position Step into the captain's chair (dip station). Rest your forearms on the pads and grip the handles firmly. Keep your back upright and close to the pad and look straight ahead. Bend your legs so that your thighs and shins form roughly a right angle. Movement Raise your knees while turning your legs slightly to one side, about 30-45 degrees, keeping your thighs parallel to the floor. Then do the same to the other side. You can pause briefly in the middle or go straight to the other side.

name: 负重颈屈
description: Weighted neck flexion is an isolation exercise designed to strengthen the anterior (front) neck flexor muscles by bringing your chin toward your chest against external resistance (most commonly a light weight plate, resistance band, or neck harness).

name: 单腿腿举
description: Strength training exercise where you push a weight away from your body using one leg at a time on a leg press machine. It helps to improve leg strength, balance, and muscular symmetry by isolating each leg individually. This exercise is particularly useful for identifying and correcting muscle imbalances between your legs.

name: 吊环上斜划船
description: Perform a row using gymnastic rings, but with the body position somewhere between vertical and horizontal. Go closer to horizontal to make it harder.

name: 泰森俯卧撑
description: Starting Position • Feet: Place the soles of your feet flat against a vertical wall, with your toes or balls of your feet on the floor. • Hands: Position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, directly under your lower chest or solar plexus. • Body: Keep your core tight, glutes squeezed, and head in a neutral position. Your knees should hover a few inches above the floor without touching it. Movement Pattern Lower Down: Flex your elbows (tucked around 45 degrees) to lower your chest toward the floor, stopping just a few centimeters short of touching the ground. Rock Back: As you press upward through your arms, push your hips backward and bend your knees, rocking your weight toward your heels while keeping your shins nearly parallel to the floor. Drive Forward: Explode forward from your lower-body/crouched position, shifting your weight back into the starting push-up plank stance to complete the repetition. Key Tips for Proper Form • Keep Knees Low: Do not let your knees or hips pike high up in the air; keep the motion low and horizontal. • Maintain Wall Contact: Keep the soles of your feet pressed against the wall so you don't lose your leverage. • Engage the Core: Avoid arching your lower back by tilting your pelvis backward and bracing your abs.

name: 手腕摇摆
description: Start on all fours with your palms flat on the floor. Slowly rock forward and backward, keeping your hands planted. Move only within a comfortable, pain-free wrist range to gently improve mobility and flexibility.

name: 肩胛俯卧撑
description: Start in a straight-arm plank with your hands under your shoulders. Keep your elbows locked and move only your shoulder blades: let your chest sink slightly, then push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades. Move in a comfortable, controlled range.

name: 哑铃自行车手深蹲
description: Dumbbell squats with elevated heel position. Stand on either squat wedges or weight plates to raise heels higher than toes, while holding the dumbbells on your sides.

name: 三头俯卧撑
description: Push ups for targeting triceps. Start with a plank position with your hands directly below your shoulders, feet together. When descending, keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Upper arms straight back. Lower until your chest touches the floor, then return.

name: 交叉拉伸
description: Extend your right arm straight across your chest toward the left. Hook your left arm around your right elbow and pull your right arm a little closer to your body. Keep your shoulder down as you do this. Repeat on the other side.

name: 手腕拉伸
description: Extend your right arm straight out in front of you, with your palm facing up (fingers pointing toward the floor). Using your left hand, gently pull the fingers of your right hand toward you until you feel a stretch in your forearm and biceps.

name: 股四头肌拉伸
description: Stand on one leg (hold onto a wall if necessary). Use your hand to grasp the ankle of your other leg and gently pull your heel toward your buttocks. Make sure your knees stay close together and that you push your pelvis slightly forward (avoid arching your back).

name: V字起身
description: One of the best exercises for the rectus abdominis muscles. Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms close to your sides. Lift your head off the floor and raise your legs and arms about 15 centimeters off the floor. Your palms should face down, and look up at the ceiling. Now bend your legs and at the same time sit up so that your knees and chest almost touch. Only your buttocks are still on the floor. Your arms are now extended at shoulder height. Then slowly return to the starting position with your arms and legs extended and your head raised.

name: 主动悬垂
description: A static hold from a pull-up bar with straight elbows and actively depressed, stabilized shoulders. Grip a secure bar and let your body hang under control. Keep your elbows straight and gently draw your shoulders down, away from your ears. Maintain this active shoulder position without pulling up, swinging, or repeatedly moving the shoulder blades. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier if your grip opens, shoulder control deteriorates, or pain occurs. Record actual seconds, grip, and any assistance used. This is distinct from a relaxed passive dead hang or a moving scapular pull-up.

name: 折刀保持（地板）
description: A static bodyweight support with both hands and feet on the floor and hips raised in a pike position. Place your hands and feet securely on the floor, then raise your hips. Keep your elbows straight and actively push the floor away through your shoulders. Maintain a controlled, stationary position without bending your elbows, lowering your head for push-up repetitions, or raising your feet onto a surface. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier for loss of alignment, loss of active shoulder support, or pain. Record actual seconds, hand and foot spacing, and alignment. This is the floor variation, not a pike push-up or an elevated-feet pike hold.

name: 呼气与体位游泳练习
description: Swim one short pool length at a gentle pace while focusing on a relaxed body position and a steady exhale into the water between breaths. Pause at the wall between lengths. This is a moving swim technique drill, not stationary bobbing or a kickboard-only exercise.

name: 靠墙肩屈拉伸
description: Place both hands against a wall above shoulder height. Step back and gently move the chest downward while reaching the arms overhead, keeping the back controlled. Hold a comfortable shoulder flexion stretch without forcing the range or arching the lower back.

name: 脚辅助直杆支撑
description: Hold a stable straight bar in front of the hips with both arms straight. Keep both feet on the floor or a stable platform so they assist your body weight. Maintain steady shoulders and a controlled supported position without swinging. This is a feet-assisted straight-bar support hold, not a ring hold or a full dip.

name: 控制快速游
description: Swim a short pool length at a controlled brisk effort, maintaining smooth strokes and steady breathing. Stop at the wall for the prescribed recovery before the next repeat. This is a submaximal swim interval, not an all-out sprint; distance, repeats and rest are set by the routine.

name: 支撑深蹲保持
description: Hold a stable support in front of you and lower into a comfortable deep squat with both feet grounded. Use the support for balance and to control depth. Maintain the squat hold without bouncing or forcing the hips or ankles farther than a comfortable range.

name: 哑铃腕上抬
description: Stand tall with your arm hanging straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle so the weighted end points forward and your thumb is on top. Keep the arm completely still and tip the weighted end up toward the ceiling using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This trains radial deviation, the riser used in arm wrestling. Slide your hand further from the weight to make it harder.

name: 腕上抬等长保持
description: Set up exactly as for dumbbell wrist rising: arm straight down by your side, dumbbell held at one end with the weight pointing forward. Tip the weight up to the top position and hold it still for the set time without letting it drop. This builds tendon strength in the riser for arm wrestling. Start light and stop if you feel sharp pain in the wrist or elbow.

name: 壶铃腕翻转
description: Rest your forearm on a bench or your knee and hold a light kettlebell by the handle with the bell hanging down. Keeping the elbow and forearm still, slowly rotate your wrist so the palm turns down, then rotate back so the palm turns up. Do the set number of turns in each direction. This trains pronation and supination for grip and arm wrestling.

name: 哑铃旋前等长保持
description: Rest your forearm on a bench with the palm facing in and the thumb on top. Hold a dumbbell by one end with the weighted end pointing up. Let the weight tip about 45 degrees toward the palm up side, then stop it and hold that position for the set time. The muscles that stop it falling are your pronators, which roll the hand over in arm wrestling. Start with a light weight because the leverage is high.

name: 腕弯举等长保持
description: Sit on a bench with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing up, holding a dumbbell or barbell. Curl the wrist all the way up and hold the top position for the set time, squeezing hard. This builds cupping strength and tendon resilience for grip and arm wrestling. Do it straight after your wrist curls without changing seats.

name: 慢速离心引体下降
description: Stand on a box or bench under a pull-up bar and step up so your chin is above the bar with your elbows fully bent. Take your feet off the box and lower yourself as slowly as you can, aiming for five seconds, until your arms are straight. Step back onto the box and repeat. This builds the strength needed for full pull-ups.

name: 引体顶端保持
description: Use a box or bench to get your chin above a pull-up bar with your elbows fully bent and shoulders pulled down. Take your feet off the box and hold that top position still for the set time. Keep your chest up and do not let your chin drop below the bar. This strengthens the hardest part of the pull-up.

name: 毛巾握悬垂
description: Hang two towels over a pull-up bar, one for each hand. Grip a towel tightly in each hand and hang with your arms straight and your shoulders active for as long as you can. The thick, unstable towels make your grip work much harder than a normal bar. This builds crushing grip strength for arm wrestling.

name: 绳索腕屈扣
description: Attach a single handle to a low cable. Rest your forearm on a bench or your thigh with the palm facing up and the cable pulling your hand away from you. Curl your fingers and wrist toward you as if cupping a ball, squeeze for a second, then lower slowly. This builds the wrist flexion used to control an opponent's hand in arm wrestling.

name: 绳索背侧压腕
description: Set a cable at chest height and stand side on, holding the handle with your elbow bent about ninety degrees in front of you, like an arm wrestling setup. Pull the handle toward your body using your biceps and back, keeping the wrist cupped, then return slowly. This trains the hook or back pressure used in arm wrestling.

name: 绳索侧向压腕
description: Set a cable at chest height and stand side on with the cable on your working side. Hold the handle with your elbow bent about ninety degrees and close to your body. Press the handle across your body toward your opposite side using your chest and shoulder, then return slowly. This trains the side pressure used to pin an opponent in arm wrestling.

name: 绳索腕旋前
description: Attach a strap or handle to a cable at hand height so the cable pulls your palm toward facing up. Keep your elbow bent at your side and still. Rotate your forearm so the palm turns down against the cable, then let it rotate back slowly. This builds pronation strength for rolling an opponent's hand in arm wrestling.

name: 绳索腕旋后
description: Attach a strap or handle to a cable at hand height so the cable pulls your palm toward facing down. Keep your elbow bent at your side and still. Rotate your forearm so the palm turns up against the cable, then let it rotate back slowly. This balances pronation work and protects the elbow.

name: 锤式杠杆
description: Hold a sledgehammer or an empty dumbbell handle with a plate on one end near the bottom of the handle, arm by your side. Using only the wrist, lift the head up in front of you, then lower it slowly. Turn around so the head is behind you to train the opposite direction. Move your hand further from the weight to make it harder.

name: 哑铃尺偏
description: Stand with your arm straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle with the weighted end pointing behind you. Keeping the arm still, lift the weighted end up behind you using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This is the opposite of wrist rising and keeps the wrist balanced.

name: 腕力卷绳器
description: Hold a wrist roller, a short bar with a rope and a small weight attached, with both hands at shoulder height and arms straight out in front. Roll the bar with your wrists to wind the rope up until the weight reaches the bar, then unwind it slowly. Roll forward and backward on different sets to train both sides of the forearm.

name: 握力器挤压
description: Hold a spring hand gripper deep in your palm. Squeeze until the handles touch, hold for a second, then open slowly. Use a gripper strength you can close for the target reps. This builds crushing grip strength for holding on in arm wrestling and in pulling exercises.

name: 弹力带伸指
description: Put a small rubber band around all five fingertips. Spread your fingers and thumb open as wide as possible against the band, hold for a second, then close slowly. This trains the extensor muscles that open the hand and balances heavy gripping, which helps keep the elbows and wrists healthy.

name: 片心提举
description: Place a weight plate on the floor with the hub facing up, or use a loading pin with a plate attached. Pinch the hub with your fingertips on one side and your thumb on the other, then stand up and hold it for the set time. This builds thumb and pinch strength, which helps grip control in arm wrestling.

name: 粗握把哑铃静持
description: Fit thick grip sleeves over two dumbbell handles, or wrap the handles in a towel to make them thicker. Stand tall holding one in each hand at your sides and hold for the set time without letting the handles roll in your hands. The thicker handle makes your fingers and thumb work much harder than a normal grip.

name: 米桶训练
description: Fill a deep bucket with dry rice. Push your hand into the rice and repeatedly open and close your fist, twist your wrist both ways, and spread your fingers against the rice for the set time. This is a low impact way to train every muscle of the hand and forearm and is good for warming up or recovery.

name: 毛巾引体向上
description: Hang two towels over a pull-up bar and grip one in each hand. Pull yourself up until your hands are near your chin, then lower slowly to straight arms. Holding the towels makes your grip work much harder than a normal pull-up. Use assistance or do negatives if you cannot do full reps yet.

name: 爬绳
description: Grip a hanging climbing rope with both hands overhead. Pull yourself up hand over hand, using your legs to clamp the rope if needed, then climb down with control. Beginners can start seated on the floor and pull up to standing. This builds pulling and grip strength together.

name: 跳跃引体向上
description: Stand under a pull-up bar on the floor or a low box so you can reach the bar with bent arms. Jump and pull at the same time until your chin passes the bar, then lower yourself as slowly as you can. This is a beginner step toward full pull-ups.

name: 倒蹬（腿举）
description: 倒蹬：坐姿有靠背，脊柱有支撑，双脚与肩同宽踩踏板，蹬到底别让骨盆翻起来，缓慢控制还原，膝盖与脚尖同向，全程保持呼吸节奏。

name: 保加利亚分腿蹲
description: 保加利亚分腿蹲：单腿、躯干直立，后脚搭凳，前腿下蹲至大腿与地面平行，膝盖与脚尖同向，不稳可扶架退阶，起身时前腿发力。

name: 臀推
description: 臀推：肩胛靠凳、脊柱有支撑，双脚踩地，臀部发力顶髋至身体成直线，顶峰收紧一秒，别过度伸髋，缓慢下放，练臀不压腰。

name: 死虫式
description: 死虫式：仰卧，腰贴地，对侧手脚同时伸展，吸气伸展、呼气还原，全程保持腰椎中立不塌腰，中立位抗伸展，练腹不压腰。

name: 鸟狗式
description: 鸟狗式：四足跪姿，对侧手脚同时伸展，骨盆保持水平，腰别塌，对侧伸展后缓慢还原，中立位抗旋转，练核心稳定性。

name: 侧支撑
description: 侧支撑：侧卧，肘撑地，骨盆、腹腔、胸椎对齐，身体成一条直线，保持呼吸，别塌腰别耸肩，练侧腹与核心抗侧屈。

name: 坐姿哑铃弯举
description: 坐姿哑铃弯举：坐姿有靠背，大臂固定贴紧身体两侧，弯举哑铃至顶峰稍停，缓慢控制下放，不要借腰甩动，全程保持肘部稳定。

name: 吊环悬垂举腿提髋
name_en: Hanging Leg Raise with Hip Lift on Rings (Custom)
description: 吊环悬垂举腿提髋：双手握吊环悬垂，先卷骨盆再抬腿并提髋，稳住躯干别摆荡，缓慢控制下放，练下腹与髋屈肌，动作全程保持控制。

name: 腰方肌拉伸
description: 腰方肌拉伸：站姿单侧侧屈，缓慢向一侧弯曲，感受腰侧拉伸，保持三十秒，换边重复，动作轻柔别用力过猛，练中有刺痛就停。

name: 抬腿外旋
name_en: Standing Leg Lift with External Rotation (Custom)
description: 抬腿外旋：站姿屈膝抬腿外展，缓慢控制，感受髋部外侧发力，每侧十次，动作平稳别晃动，扶墙保持平衡也可以，练髋部活动度。

name: 俯身蹬腿
description: 俯身蹬腿：俯卧双腿伸直，交替或双腿向后蹬，臀部收紧，腰别塌，动作缓慢控制，十次一组，练臀部与腰背协同发力。

name: 死虫式呼吸
description: 死虫式呼吸：仰卧，吸满气、肋骨下沉、腰贴地，缓慢呼气保持腹内压，五次一组，练前重建腹内压，先重建再上重量，呼吸节奏均匀。

name: 直腿腘绳肌拉伸
description: Lie on your back with both legs extended. Raise one leg straight up and gently pull it towards your upper body with both hands around your thigh. Keep the knee as straight as possible and your lower back on the mat. Hold the stretch, then switch legs.

name: 俯身划船
description: Standing with the torso bent forward from the hips at roughly 45 degrees, back straight. Hold two dumbbells with an overhand grip, arms hanging below the shoulders. Pull the dumbbells along the body toward the pelvis, elbows close to the torso, briefly squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top. Lower under control. Primary muscle: lats. Keep the torso stable throughout the movement, no arching of the lower back.

name: TRX/吊环飞鸟
description: Set TRX straps or rings at about mid-chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor. Hold one handle or ring in each hand, palms facing each other. Step forward into a lean so the straps are taut, arms nearly straight in front of the chest with a slight bend in the elbows. Brace the core and glutes so the body forms one straight line from head to heels. Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears. Keeping the same elbow bend, open the arms out to the sides in a wide arc and let the body lower forward. Stop when the hands are roughly level with the shoulders and you feel a stretch across the chest. Do not let the hands travel behind the body line. Squeeze the chest to bring the arms back together in front of you, raising the body to the start. Exhale as the hands meet, pause briefly, and repeat. Difficulty is set by foot position: feet closer to the anchor and a steeper lean make the movement harder; a more upright stance makes it easier. The same pattern works on a suspension trainer or gymnastics rings.

name: TRX/吊环俯卧撑
description: Set TRX straps or rings so the handles hang just above the floor, or at a height that allows a full push-up range with your feet on the ground. Grip one handle or ring in each hand. Get into a plank with the body in one straight line from head to heels, arms extended, and the straps vertical under the shoulders. Brace the core and glutes. Keep the wrists neutral and the shoulders packed down away from the ears. Bend the elbows and lower the chest between the hands until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor or you reach a comfortable depth. Keep the elbows at roughly 45 degrees from the torso; do not flare them fully out to the sides. Press through the hands to extend the arms and return to the plank. Exhale on the way up, pause briefly at the top with control, and repeat. On rings, keep the rings close to the body so they do not drift wide. Difficulty increases if the feet are elevated or the straps are set lower so the body is more horizontal; a higher handle position makes it easier.

name: TRX/吊环Y举
description: Set TRX straps or rings at about mid-chest to waist height. Stand facing the anchor and hold one handle or ring in each hand. Walk the feet toward the anchor and lean back until the arms are extended in front of you and the body forms a straight line from head to heels. Palms face each other or slightly down. Brace the core and glutes. Keep the shoulders down and the ribs stacked over the pelvis. With a soft bend in the elbows, raise the arms up and out into a Y shape overhead, so the hands finish roughly in line with the ears and wider than the shoulders. Reach long through the arms without shrugging. Pause briefly at the top with control. Lower the arms under control back to the start position in front of the body, then repeat. Keep tension in the straps throughout. A more upright stance makes the movement easier; a deeper lean makes it harder.

name: TRX/吊环面拉
description: Set TRX straps or rings at about head to mid-chest height. Stand facing the anchor and hold one handle or ring in each hand with a neutral grip. Walk the feet toward the anchor and lean back until the arms are extended in front of you and the body forms a straight line from head to heels. Brace the core and glutes. Soften the knees slightly and keep the ribs down. Pull the handles or rings toward the face by driving the elbows high and wide, roughly to ear height. Externally rotate the shoulders so the hands finish near the temples or just outside the ears, thumbs pointing back if the straps allow. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without shrugging toward the ears. Pause briefly. Extend the arms under control back to the start and repeat. Keep constant tension in the straps. A steeper lean increases difficulty; a more upright stance makes it easier.

name: TRX/吊环臂屈伸
description: Set TRX straps or rings so the handles hang at a height that lets you support your body with straight arms and the feet clear of the floor, or lightly assisted if needed. Grip one handle or ring in each hand. Jump or step into a support hold: arms locked out, shoulders packed down, chest up, and the body tight from head to heels. On rings, turn the palms slightly inward (rings turned out) for a stable lockout. Brace the core and lean the torso slightly forward. Bend the elbows and lower under control until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or to a depth you can reverse without shoulder pain. Keep the elbows close to the body rather than flaring wide. On rings, keep the rings close to the sides so they do not drift outward. Press through the hands to extend the arms and return to the support hold. Exhale on the way up, pause briefly at the top with full lockout, and repeat. Assisted variations: keep the feet on the floor or a box and use the legs lightly. Harder variations: slower eccentrics, pauses at the bottom, or a more forward lean for more chest emphasis.

name: 弹跳小跳
description: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. Perform quick, low vertical jumps using primarily your ankles. Keep your torso upright, minimise knee bending and aim for short ground contact times. Land on the balls of your feet and immediately rebound into the next jump.

name: 下蹲反向跳
description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Quickly bend your knees and hips into a shallow squat, then immediately extend your hips, knees and ankles to jump as high as possible. Use a natural arm swing to assist the jump. Land softly with both feet, absorb the impact and reset before the next repetition.

name: 助跑起跳
description: Start a few steps away from your takeoff point. Perform a controlled two- or three-step approach, increasing speed progressively. Plant your foot or feet firmly and jump vertically as high as possible using an explosive arm swing. Land under control, regain balance and reset before repeating.

name: 立定跳远
description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Swing your arms backwards while bending your knees and hips. Explosively extend your lower body and swing your arms forwards to jump as far as possible. Land on both feet with your knees bent, maintain balance and reset before the next repetition.

name: 侧向跳稳定落地
description: Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent. Push explosively sideways and jump towards the opposite leg. Land on that leg with your knee and hip slightly bent. Hold the landing position for one to two seconds while maintaining balance and proper knee alignment. Repeat in the opposite direction.

name: 单臂背包划船
description: Stand with your feet staggered and bend forward at the hips, keeping your back neutral. Hold a securely closed, weighted backpack by a strong handle with one hand. Support your free hand on your thigh for stability. Pull the backpack towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body. Slowly lower the backpack to the starting position without rotating your torso. Complete all repetitions before switching arms.
